notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.entry: For three vectors $E_1,E_2,E_3$ in Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ and a linear map $B$, the formal entry is $E_i\cdot BE_j$. With an orthonormal frame these are the matrix components $B_{ij}$ of Lemma 2.2; in particular $\nu=B_{12}$ and $\eta=B_{32}$. The supplied formula itself does not require orthonormality or trace zero. Its coordinate positions are numbered from zero, so the first, second and third positions correspond to the paper’s subscripts $1,2,3$. No transpose or interchange of row and column is involved.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.frame: Given paths $k_p,\mathbf a_p$ in Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$, the formal frame is $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$, as in §1.1 and Lemma 2.2. This definition alone does not assert orthonormality: that requires both vectors to be nonzero and perpendicular. Normalization assigns the zero vector to a zero input, so a vanishing wave vector or amplitude still produces a defined triple but not an orthonormal frame. Its three positions correspond, in order, to the paper’s axes $E_1,E_2,E_3$.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.hasDerivWith: Let $f$ be a vector-valued path whose derivative at $t_0+\tau/r$, relative to a time set $I$, is $v$. Suppose $s\mapsto t_0+s/r$ maps the chosen normalized time set $J$ into $I$. The formal statement gives derivative $v/r$ for $s\mapsto f(t_0+s/r)$ relative to $J$ at $\tau$. This includes the one-sided derivatives at interval endpoints used in §2.2.1. It does not require $r\ne0$: division by zero is assigned zero, making the reparametrized path constant when $r=0$. The application has $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}>0$.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.movingFrame_: At a time $t$ in a time set $I$, let $B:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ have trace zero. Suppose $\kappa(t),\mathbf a(t)$ are nonzero and perpendicular, with $\kappa_t=-B^T\kappa$ and $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)B\mathbf a$ there, taking derivatives within $I$. Form $E_1=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $E_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$ and $E_3=E_1\times E_2$. Each $E_i$ has a derivative within $I$ whose Euclidean norm is at most $2\|B\|$. The matrix norm is the operator norm. The statement is pointwise and requires no bound on $B_t$; a uniform bound for $B$ gives the displayed interval estimate in §6.2.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.normalized_r: Let $k_p,\mathbf a_p$ be nonzero both at time zero and at time $t$, and let $r\ne0$. Put $\sigma=|k_p(0)||\mathbf a_p(0)|$, $\sigma_p(t)=|k_p(t)||\mathbf a_p(t)|$ and $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$. The formal identity is $(\sigma/r)(\sigma_p/\sigma)E_2\otimes E_1=(\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p)/r$. Multiplication by $r$ recovers the preceding-wave term in $M$ in §2.2.1. This algebra does not require perpendicularity or an evolution equation. Time zero here is the chosen base time; the physical application shifts it to $t_0$.

Let $I$ be compact and contain $t_0$, with a continuous frame orthonormal at $t_0$, continuous matrices $B,E_c$, $\sigma>0$, and positive frozen entries $
u=B_{12}(t_0)$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)$ satisfying $\eta/
u\le1$. Put $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, and put $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$, with $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. The formal statement proves $\delta\ge0$, $S^{-1}\le2\delta$, and, for every $t\in I$, $\|B/r\|\le\delta$, $\|E_c/r\|\le\delta/S$, $|B_{12}/
u-1|\le\delta$, $|B_{32}/
u-\eta/
u|\le\delta$. Operator norms are Euclidean. No wave evolution is needed for this estimate; compactness and continuity make the suprema finite.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.normalized_w: At a time in a set $J$, let $(E_1,E_2,E_3)$ be orthonormal, $b_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $d_{ij}=E_i\cdot EE_j$. Assume $E_1'=-b_{12}E_2-b_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=b_{12}E_1-b_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=b_{13}E_1+b_{32}E_2$, and $k'=-M^Tk$, where $M=B+ScE_2\otimes E_1+E$. For $\lambda,S\ne0$, define $(X,Q,Z)=(E_1\cdot k,SE_2\cdot k,E_3\cdot k)/\lambda$. The formal statement gives $X'=-b_{11}X-[c+(b_{21}+b_{12})/S]Q-(b_{31}+b_{13})Z-d_{11}X-d_{21}Q/S-d_{31}Z$, $Q'=-b_{22}Q-2Sb_{32}Z-Sd_{12}X-d_{22}Q-Sd_{32}Z$, and $Z'=-b_{33}Z-(b_{23}-b_{32})Q/S-d_{13}X-d_{23}Q/S-d_{33}Z$. Derivatives are relative to $J$. Here $(X,Q,Z)=\zeta$ in the paper; normalized physical time uses $B/r,E_c/r$ and $c=\sigma_p/\sigma$. The identity assumes no smallness, trace condition or nonvanishing of $k$.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.polynomial_w: Let $0\le\varepsilon\le1$, $T\ge2$ and $D\ge0$, with $12DT^3\le1$. On $[0,T]$, suppose $(X,Q,Z)(0)=(0,0,1)$ and $X'=-Q+r_1$, $Q'=-\varepsilon Z+r_2$, $Z'=r_3$, where each $|r_i|\le D(|X|+|Q|+|Z|)$. The formal statement gives $|X-\varepsilon\tau^2/2|+|Q+\varepsilon\tau|+|Z-1|\le24DT^5$ for every $\tau\in[0,T]$. It uses the sum of absolute coordinate errors, which bounds their Euclidean norm. This supplies the perturbative estimate behind (2.10), conditional on these residual bounds; it does not itself obtain them from the physical gradients.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.scaled_waveV: At a fixed time, let $(E_1,E_2,E_3)$ be orthonormal and let $\lambda,S\ne0$. Define the coordinates by $\zeta_1=(k\cdot E_1)/\lambda$, $\zeta_2=S(k\cdot E_2)/\lambda$, $\zeta_3=(k\cdot E_3)/\lambda$. The formal statement proves $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$, the wave-vector part of (2.3). The assertion is pointwise linear algebra and includes $k=0$. It neither assumes the wave equation nor constructs an amplitude. Nonzero scales are required because the reconstruction cancels the divisions used in the coordinates.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.strengthRati: On $[0,T]$, suppose $k_p,\mathbf a_p$ are nonzero, perpendicular paths satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$ over trace-free $B$, with Euclidean operator norm $\|B(t)\|\le\delta$ and $T\delta\le1$. The formal statement proves $|\sigma_p(t)/\sigma_p(0)-1|\le2T\delta$, where $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$. This is the strength estimate used in Lemma 2.4, after time normalization makes $B$ the physical background divided by $r$. The denominator is positive by the initial nonvanishing assumptions. Only relative derivatives on the interval are needed; smoothness of $B$ is not an additional hypothesis.
notes.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.waveVector_c: Let $0\le\varepsilon\le1/2$, $T\ge2$, $0\le\tau\le T$, and assume $|X-\varepsilon\tau^2/2|+|Q+\varepsilon\tau|+|Z-1|\le1/2$. The formal statement gives $1/2\le Z\le3/2$, $|X|\le T^2$, $|Q|\le T$ and $X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2\ge1/4$. These are algebraic consequences of the error bound, before any amplitude equation is used. The conclusion holds for every real $S$, because division by zero is assigned zero and the $Z^2$ term already supplies the lower bound. In the physical application $S>0$ and the last expression is $m$ in (2.3).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AdmissibleThreshold: For a nonnegative integer $b$ and functions $F,\mathcal B$ on the nonnegative integers, the formal condition requires, at positive indices, that $\mathcal B$ be nondecreasing, positive, at least $F$, and satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$, where $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. Values at zero are unrestricted. The function $F$ is a proposed majorant of the fixed-order analytic constants; the inequality $F(s)\le\mathcal B(s)$ alone does not identify those constants or prove that $F$ bounds them. The condition also does not itself require $b\ge1$. Those facts must be supplied in the application to the parameter choice of §1.5.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AmplitudeVector: For a prescribed wave vector $k$ on a compact physical time set $I$, the formal condition requires $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ and $\mathbf a\cdot k=0$ at every time in $I$, where $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$. Derivatives are taken relative to $I$. This is the amplitude vector of §2.2.1; no initial amplitude or nonvanishing condition is imposed, and the zero solution is allowed. The formula assigns zero to division by zero. Its physical use accompanies a launched wave vector that is nonzero on the active interval, so that convention does not alter the pressure coefficient there.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixB.CutoffSymbol: The formal object is a smooth function $\psi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $0\le\psi\le1$, $\psi(\zeta)=1$ for $|\zeta|\le1$, $\psi(\zeta)=0$ for $|\zeta|>2$, and $\psi(-\zeta)=\psi(\zeta)$. Thus its support is compact and contained in the closed ball of radius two. Appendix B assumes radiality; the formal condition requires only evenness, which admits additional symbols. This is a condition on the symbol, not the definition of the operator $S_\Lambda$ or a proof of any operator estimate. No frequency parameter or field is selected here.
Suppose $\psi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ is smooth, takes values in $[0,1]$, equals one on the unit ball, vanishes outside the ball of radius two, and has equal values at points with equal Euclidean norm. The formal statement shows that $\psi$ satisfies the cutoff conditions used in Appendix B. The only deduction is evenness, since $|-\zeta|=|\zeta|$; all other conditions are supplied as hypotheses. It therefore verifies that every radial symbol allowed by the paper is allowed by the formalization, without asserting that an even symbol must be radial.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.CoefficientPo: For $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$, with $X$ a real normed space, this condition requires smoothness in the label variable, bounded derivatives uniformly over the specified time set $I$, and $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$ for every $m\ge0$. The sequence $(C_m)$ is an explicit input, and $q$ is a nonnegative integer. The quantity $|c|_m$ is the sum of the suprema of the coordinate derivatives with $|\beta|=m$. In Lemma D.2 the output constants are chosen before $I$, $\mathsf D$ and the fields, which supplies the paper's uniformity. This condition by itself imposes no lower bound on $\mathsf D$; the coefficient estimates separately assume $\mathsf D\ge1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.coefficientOr: For a phase-independent field $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$, this expression is $|c|_m=\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{t\in I,a\in\mathbb R^3}|\partial_a^\beta c(t,a)|$, with the norm of the real normed target space $X$. A sorted list of coordinate differentiations represents each multi-index once. The supremum includes all times in the chosen set, not time derivatives; choosing $I=[t_0,T]$ gives the paper's interval. The expression uses real-valued suprema, so the separate boundedness hypotheses are needed for it to measure the derivatives. It does not assert smoothness or boundedness of an arbitrary coefficient.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm: For $f(t,a,s)$, $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, the expression sums the suprema of $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^jf$ over $|\beta|+j\le n$, counting each pair $(\beta,j)$ once. The supremum runs over the entire chosen time set, all labels and all phases. For positive scales and bounded smooth derivatives this is $\|f\|_{[n]}$ in (D.1); for a periodic profile the phase supremum may equivalently be taken over one period. The expression itself neither requires periodicity nor proves boundedness. Smoothness and boundedness are separate assumptions in the estimates that use it, and there are no time derivatives in this norm.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm_pha: Let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in its spatial variable at every time, let $\ell_*\ge0$, and let $n\ge0$ be an integer. Regarding $c(t,a)$ as a function of $(t,a,s)$ independent of $s$, the formal statement gives $\|c\|_{[n]}=\sum_{m=0}^n\ell_*^m|c|_m$ for every real phase weight $h$. Every derivative containing a phase differentiation is zero, so only spatial multi-indices remain. This identifies the two expressions used in Appendix D. Boundedness is not a hypothesis of this identity between expressions; it must be supplied separately when interpreting them as finite derivative norms.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.holderFieldNo: For a phase-independent field $c(t,a)$, this expression is the sum over $|\beta|\le n$ of the uniform-in-time half-Hölder norms of $\ell_*^{|\beta|}\partial_a^\beta c$. Labels range over $\mathbb R^3$ and there is no time differentiation. Each half-Hölder norm is the maximum of the spatial supremum and $\sup_{a\ne b}|g(a)-g(b)|/|a-b|^{1/2}$. The coincident-point quotient is assigned zero. The customary sum of these two quantities is between this maximum and twice it. The paper does not specify that internal convention; the distinction changes constants, not the boundedness class. Boundedness of all quantities entering the expression is a separate hypothesis.

Let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, with $X$ a real normed space, and let $\ell_*\ge0$. For every integer $n\ge0$, the formal statement identifies the finite Hölder expression with $\sum_{m=0}^n\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}$. Each multi-index occurs once, and each order uses the supremum over all times in $I$ of the maximum of the spatial supremum and half-Hölder seminorm. The equality is the grouping by order stated in Appendix D. It does not establish finiteness; bounded derivative and difference-quotient families must be assumed when these expressions are used as norms.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.holderOrderNo: For a phase-independent field $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$, the formal expression sums, over $|\beta|=m$, the supremum in time of the maximum of $\|\partial_a^\beta c(t)\|_\infty$ and its spatial half-Hölder seminorm. Each multi-index is counted once. Difference quotients use Euclidean distances between labels; the quotient at equal labels is assigned zero. The paper's notation $|c|_{m,1/2}$ does not specify whether the two parts of the Hölder norm are added or maximized. Replacing the maximum by their sum changes this quantity by at most a factor two. Smoothness and boundedness are not conclusions of the definition.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weightedField: For a field $f(t,a,s)$ and a time-dependent scalar $\gamma(t)$, this expression is the mixed finite norm of $f(t,a,s)/\gamma(t)$: it sums $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j\sup|\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^j(f/\gamma)|$ over $|\beta|+j\le n$. All suprema include the chosen time set, labels and phases; only labels and phases are differentiated. The paper assumes $\gamma(t)>0$ on $[t_0,T]$, and the numbered estimates impose that assumption. The definition alone allows zero weights: at a time with $\gamma(t)=0$, the normalized field is assigned zero. Thus the expression alone cannot certify the paper's positive-amplitude normalization or the finiteness of its derivative bounds.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.MixedIncrementBound: Fix a stage $j$ and nonnegative integers $m,q$. Set $w(t,x)=\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)(t,x)$, differentiating at fixed $x$ within $[0,S_j]$. The formal condition requires finiteness of the spatial Hölder measurement, its bound $\|w(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for every $t$, and continuity of $t\mapsto w(t)$ in that norm. Thus it includes the meaning of the time-space norm in auxiliary equation (1.2), not merely a pointwise estimate. The spatial norm's defining formula is absent; accompanying comments describe operator norms of spatial derivatives. At $j=0$, the predecessor index is also zero because natural-number subtraction stops at zero. The auxiliary lemma uses this condition only eventually.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Proof.theorem_1_1_o: The authors' source records this statement as not proved and outside the main argument; neither formal main theorem uses it. Assume Theorem 7.1, Propositions 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4, Corollary 8.3, and the generalized mixed estimate for every qualifying construction. For each cutoff symbol and integer $a_0$, the conclusion chooses integers $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and majorants $F,G$. Thresholds satisfying the main conditions for $F$ and $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$, with $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, exist; every such threshold yields a solution for all sufficiently large initial frequencies. The solution has bounded velocity, the main vorticity blow-up and integral conclusions, uniqueness among maximal solutions of finite lifespan with the same initial data, and a smooth periodic velocity extension through its terminal time off $\mathbb Z^3$. Euler is imposed only before that time. This is a proved implication. The authors' formalization marks its generalized mixed estimate as not proved; a separate selected construction proves the existence conclusion.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_2: The authors' source records this statement as not proved and outside the main argument; neither formal main theorem uses it. For each cutoff symbol, the formal statement asks for $a_0$ such that each integer $a\ge a_0$ has a majorant $G$, chosen before the construction. Every sequence satisfying the specified Section 7 step data, strength $18e^3$, and $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$ must then satisfy $\|\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)\|_{C([0,S_j];C^{m,1/2})}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ eventually for every fixed $(m,q)$. Time derivatives fix the physical point; continuity in the spatial norm is included. The majorant also covers the main fixed-order constants used by this argument. This quantifies over every qualifying construction, whereas the paper discusses its selected one. The authors' formalization states this assertion and marks it as not proved; the separately proved selected-construction result has narrower quantifiers.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_3: The authors' source records this statement as not proved and outside the main argument; neither formal main theorem uses it. For each cutoff symbol and every sufficiently large integer envelope exponent $a$, the formal statement asks for a majorant $G$ chosen before the construction. For every sequence with the specified Section 7 data, strength $18e^3$, and threshold dominating $G(7K(s))$, it then asks that each $q$ admit integers $\psi_q,j_q$ such that, for $j\ge j_q$ and $i\le q$, $\|\partial_t^iU_j\|_{C_tL^\infty}\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $\|\partial_t^iR_j\|_{C_tL^\infty}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$. Both time curves must be continuous in the supremum norm on $[0,S_j]$. The exponents and starting indices come after the construction. The authors' formalization marks this universal formulation as not proved; the selected-construction theorem proves the auxiliary estimate with narrower quantifiers.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1: The authors' source records this statement as not proved and outside the main argument; neither formal main theorem uses it. For every cutoff symbol and every lower bound on the integer envelope exponent, this formal statement asks for exponents $b,a$ and majorants $F,G$. Suitable thresholds $\mathcal B$ must exist, and every threshold satisfying both majorants must produce, for every sufficiently large initial frequency, a common sequence and a finite-time singular Euler solution. The solution retains bounded velocity, central vorticity divergence, divergent gradient and vorticity integrals, spatial limits off the origin, and uniqueness among maximal solutions of finite lifespan with the same initial data. Its periodic velocity must extend smoothly through the terminal time off $\mathbb Z^3$; Euler is imposed only before it. The authors' formalization marks this generalized assertion as not proved. Its selected-construction existence theorem and the proved main Remark 1.2 establish the required existence of a strengthened solution.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeBounds: For a specified stage $j$ and nonnegative integers $q,\psi_q$, the condition requires, for every $i\le q$, $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$. It also requires continuity of both time curves in the spatial supremum norm. The fields are periodic lifts, so this is the intended $C([0,S_j];L^\infty)$ meaning of auxiliary equation (1.3). Derivatives fix $x$ and are one-sided at the endpoints. The exponent is an integer, not the cutoff symbol. This condition concerns one stage; it neither selects the exponent nor asserts that the estimates hold eventually.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeDerivativeThres: For a nonnegative integer $b$ and functions $G,\mathcal B$ on the nonnegative integers, the formal condition is $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$ for every $s\ge1$, with $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. The argument of $G$ is therefore the largest derivative order and depth admitted by the auxiliary estimate. This condition alone does not require either function to be monotone or positive, and does not assert the main logarithmic lower bound for $\mathcal B$. Those properties enter through separate schedule or admissibility assumptions. The generalized auxiliary statements choose $G$ before the construction; its existence as a suitable analytic majorant is not supplied by this inequality itself.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear: Given functions $M(t,a)$, $\kappa(t,a)$, $\mathbf a_c(t)$ and $\mathbf a(t,a)$, and real parameters $t_0,T,\ell_*,\mathsf D,C$, this condition requires the following for $t\in[t_0,T]$ and $|a|\le2\ell_*$: $|\mathbf a(t,a)-\mathbf a_c(t)|\le C|a||\mathbf a_c(t)|$, $\tfrac12|\mathbf a_c(t)|\le|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a_c(t)|$, $(2\mathsf D)^{-1}|\kappa(t,0)||\mathbf a_c(t)|\le\kappa(t,a)\cdot M(t,a)\mathbf a(t,a)$, $\kappa(t,a)\cdot M(t,a)\mathbf a(t,a)>0$, and $(8\mathsf D)^{-1}\le\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a/(|\kappa||\mathbf a|)$. The constant $C$ is supplied, not chosen by this definition. No smoothness or seed equation is imposed here. The paper's application has $\mathsf D\ge2$ and positive radius; unrestricted reciprocals at zero are assigned zero. The condition includes more than (5.19), but does not require $C$ to be a uniform power of $\mathsf D$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti: The fields are smooth phase-periodic profiles on $[0,T]$, compatible with the same label translations and with the same transported nonzero covector. Two transverse solutions with the same source, zero initial velocity and zero-mean pressure agree. The homogeneous ordinary differential equation eliminates their velocity difference; pressure normalization then removes the remaining phase-constant difference. This proves the uniqueness asserted in §5.4 and transfers bounds for the chosen solution to every solution covered by Lemma 5.3. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.levelSource_eq_s: Here $C_p$ means the correction generated by $V_{p-1}$, although the stored correction is indexed by its generating velocity. For each retained level $p\le P$, the source written with the level sums in (5.26) agrees with the source used by the finite recursion. The proof reconciles the interaction ranges and assigns each curl correction to the following level. At level two, obtaining the special expression (5.25) additionally uses the leading-wave activation identity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Corollary83Conclusions: For prescribed $T,u,p$, these are the requirements of Corollary 8.3, not an existence proof. The velocity and mean-zero pressure solve smooth periodic Euler on $[0,T)$, where $0<T<\infty$, and have no smooth Euler continuation agreeing with the velocity there. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$ must have the same terminal time $T$. Both $\int_0^T\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_0^T\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ are infinite. The formalization uses nonnegative Lebesgue integrals and essential suprema on $[-1/2,1/2]^3$; the gradient has its operator norm. No equation is imposed at $t=T$, and no value at that time contributes to either integral.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.EndpointSystemSolution: On $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$, let $z,v$ be divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}$ fields, $c$ a time-independent field in the same space, and $G$ a vector field. The condition requires continuous $v,G$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, and $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, where $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. At each time, $G=\nabla_a\phi$ for a periodic scalar potential. Divergence is understood weakly; the spatial norm is the maximum of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm. The functions are defined for all real times. Continuity, derivative and equation requirements concern $[0,T]$; the endpoint equalities are imposed for every $T$. The condition itself does not require $T>0$; the endpoint inverse uses a positive interval, with one-sided derivatives at its ends. No normalization or time regularity of $\phi$ is imposed. This specifies the solution class of (4.9); it proves neither existence nor uniqueness.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.FiniteSmallness:
For the preceding wave, set $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$ and $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. On a compact physical set $I$, let $\delta=\|B_{12}/
u-1\|_\infty+\|B_{32}/\eta-1\|_\infty+\|B\|_\infty/r+\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$, using Euclidean matrix operator norms. The formal condition is exactly $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. Here $C_0$ is a nonnegative integer; the condition alone permits $C_0=0$ and does not require $T\ge2$. The lemmas separately impose a sufficiently large absolute lower bound on $C_0$ and $T\ge2$. If $I$ exceeds the physical interval corresponding to $[0,T]$, its larger suprema are used.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.FreezingConclusion: Let $\mathcal R$ be a bounded projection on $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;H)$ and $B$ a bounded operator-valued half-Hölder field. This condition says that $v\mapsto\mathcal R(Bv)$ is a bounded isomorphism on $\{v:\mathcal Rv=v\}$, with $\|v\|\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p\|\mathcal R(Bv)\|$, where $p$ is a nonnegative integer. For each $k\ge1$ for which $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, it requires preservation of that class in both directions and a common finite bound for the forward and inverse higher norms. Here $C,\mu,L$ are parameters: this condition does not itself impose their positivity, a Lipschitz inequality, or coercivity. Those are hypotheses of Lemma A.2, which proves the condition. Higher norms concern all spatial derivatives through the specified order; they are distinct from the base half-Hölder norm.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_threshol: Given any nonnegative integer $b$ and real functions $F,G$ on the nonnegative integers, the formal statement constructs a common threshold. One choice in the proof is $\mathcal B(s)=\exp(4K(s+1)^3)+\sum_{t=0}^s(|F(t)|+|G(7K(t))|)$, where $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. It is positive and nondecreasing, dominates the main majorant and $G(7K(s))$, and satisfies the required logarithmic lower bound. No monotonicity or positivity of $F,G$ is assumed. This proves that the two numerical threshold requirements can be met simultaneously. It does not establish that the prescribed majorants bound the analytic constants of a particular construction.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_2_of_co: Assume the main order-growth lemma, the generalized auxiliary time bounds, and a uniform implication that advances the parent time bounds to the child's mixed correction bound. The formal statement deduces the generalized auxiliary Lemma 1.2: for each fixed $(m,q)$, the correction eventually has size at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ in $C([0,S_j];C^{m,1/2})$, for every construction covered by the chosen threshold and step conditions. The threshold may be enlarged to satisfy all assumptions before choosing the construction. The analytic correction implication is an explicit hypothesis, as is the generalized time lemma. This declaration organizes those assumptions; it does not independently prove them or transfer the selected-construction theorem to all constructions.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_3_of_co: Assume a uniform implication that, for every qualifying construction and all sufficiently late stages, turns the parent bounds through order $q$ into child velocity and residual bounds through order $q+1$. The formal statement then obtains the generalized auxiliary Lemma 1.3, including time continuity in the spatial supremum norm. For each fixed $q$ and construction, one integer exponent and one starting stage work for all $i\le q$. The common implication is a mathematical hypothesis of this result, not a conclusion. The authors' formalization records this implication as an open input and does not prove it for every construction quantified over by the generalized lemma; the separate selected-construction argument has more specific hypotheses.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE: Assume a common sequence with the lifetime, support and estimates of Theorem 7.1, and an Euler solution $u,p$ with the convergence and initial-data conclusions of Proposition 8.1. notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.wave_norm_compa: Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $\tau\ge2/\varepsilon$, $\lambda>0$, and $K\ge0$. Put $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ and $\cos\varphi=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$. notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.fixedTime42: On $I=[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, let $U$ be smooth, unit-periodic and divergence free, $X$ its flow from time zero, $F=D_aX$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, and $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. The forward matrix and gradient in this assertion come from the actual flow; the input inverse assertion permits general coercive Lipschitz coefficients.

Assume that the forward map preserves $C^{k,1/2}$, that every datum in that class has a unique preimage there, and that forward and inverse norm bounds have already been proved. Then $v\in C^{k,1/2}$ if and only if $ev\in C^{k,1/2}$, and one nonnegative constant controls both norm inequalities. This is an assembly step for Lemma A.2; it makes no deduction of those analytic premises from coercivity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integral_norm_: Let $0<T\le1$, $F_t=MF$, $GF=I$, $\|G\|\le D$, and $\|M\|\le L$, with $D,L\ge0$, continuous $M$ and differentiable $F$ on $[0,T]$. notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lemma_5_3_of_le: Assume Proposition 5.1, Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2 and the weighted derivative estimate for linear ordinary differential equations supplied by Lemma D.3. The formal implication then proves Lemma 5.3. The parent on $0<T\le1$ is smooth, odd, periodic and divergence free, with $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, gradient and deformation bounds $\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. For every ordered derivative of length at most $N$, assume the initial value divided by $g(l)$ is bounded by $B$, the forcing divided by $g(t)$ by $H$, and every positive-order coefficient derivative by $C$, uniformly on $S$. Here $K,B,H,C\ge0$. Then on $[l,r]\times S$ each solution derivative satisfies $\|\partial^w x(t,p)\|/g(t)\le\Phi_N(K(r-l)C)K(B+(r-l)H)$. notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_pressu: Fix $N\in\mathbb N$ and nonnegative constants $W_j$. Assume Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2 and the weighted derivative recurrence supplied by Lemma D.3. There is $C\ge1$, fixed before these coefficients and scales, such that every derivative of order $0\le j\le N$ of the three rescaled coefficients $c(\ell_*a)$ is bounded respectively by $C\mathsf D$, $C\mathsf D^2$ and $C\mathsf D^4$. notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_A_bound: Fix a real prefactor $C$, a nonnegative integer $p$, real sequences $C_K,C_\Omega$, and nonnegative integers $a_K,a_\Omega$. notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve: Assume a common sequence with the smoothness, frequency schedule, residual, support and increment bounds of Theorem 7.1, and a smooth Euler limit $u$ with the earlier-interval convergence of Proposition 8.1. Periodicity of the approximations identifies this with the closed torus slab. The proof uses $\|U_j-U_{j-1}\|_\infty\le2\lambda_j^{-1}$ and summability of the reciprocal frequencies. Unlike the declaration that merely selects the Section 8 construction, this result includes the closed-interval limit. It asserts continuity at the origin at the terminal time, not spatial smoothness there.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveOrig: For every real $\rho$, every $T\ge0$ and every $\lambda>0$, the formal theorem constructs nonzero perpendicular paths $\kappa,\mathbf a$ solving the central wave equations over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ on $[0,T]$. They start with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$ and $\mathbf a(0)=c e_2$, $c>0$, and attain $\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|=\lambda^{-3/4}$. The proof verifies explicit paths and rescales their positive maximum. The mathematical existence conclusion agrees with the other first-wave existence theorem; using explicit formulas is a difference of proof, not of statement. No short-interval condition is needed for existence, and $T=0$ is permitted. At $T=0$, derivatives within the singleton interval impose no evolution equation beyond the stipulated values.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.first_couplin: Assume the frame identities of Lemma 2.2. Let the first central wave over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ start with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$ and amplitude in the positive $e_2$ direction, and remain nonzero and transverse on $[0,T]$. The proof obtains $|E_1'|,|E_2'|\le\|B_\rho\|$ and a coupling variation of at most $2t\|B_\rho\|^2$. Only the final positivity bound is stated as the conclusion. The formal assumption on $\rho$ allows negative values and zero as well as the paper's range.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.proposition82: Assume Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.4 and B.1, a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, and its smooth odd Euler limit $u$ from Proposition 8.1. Then $\sup_{0\le t<T_\infty}\|u(t)\|_\infty<\infty$ and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$. More precisely, there are fixed real $c>0,C$ such that, for every sufficiently large $j$ and every $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$. The constants precede the choice of $j$ and $t$. This estimate concerns the limiting solution, whereas (8.2) concerns $U_j$ and retains $\lambda_{j-2}^9$. The extra conclusion is used with crossing-time bounds to prove integral divergence. The supremum norm is the essential supremum over one spatial period.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o: Let $v:\mathbb R^3\to X$ be differentiable, where $X$ is a real normed space. The hypotheses are actual pointwise bounds, so no unproved supremum finiteness is implicit.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.MeanParentFlow: The setting is $0<T\le1$ and a velocity $u$ smooth on the closed slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, periodic under integer translations and divergence free. A supplied family $X_{s,t}$ is the particle flow of $u$. The paper's map is $X(t,a)=X_{0,t}(a)$, while $X_{t,0}$ is the reverse map. Thus the domain is $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, represented by periodic lifts. This precisely records the standing setting of §4; no Euler equation or bound on $H^\#$ is included here.

The remainder is bounded by $C_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. All derivative orders apply to the same profiles; the parent exponent is independent of order, level and depth. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: Assuming Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.5–2.7, 5.8–5.10, 6.1 and B.1 and Propositions 2.8, 5.4 and 5.11, the formal theorem derives Theorem 7.1. For each admissible radial cutoff and integer floor $a_0$, it chooses integers $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and a majorant of the fixed-order constants. Every admissible threshold $\mathcal B$ above that majorant then permits the construction for all sufficiently large initial frequencies $N$. The resulting smooth odd periodic velocities have the residual, flow, pressure, central-wave and increment bounds of (T1)–(T4), with positive common time and $C=18e^3$. It also supplies the actual expansion and truncation of each step. The central covector is still not identified with the localized step's transported covector; the first-wave direction and attained normalization are not part of this exported conclusion.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of: Assume the two inverse assertions of Lemma A.2. On $I=[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$, let $K$ be symmetric and $\Omega$ skew-symmetric, continuous in time in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatially differentiable, and uniformly bounded with their first spatial derivatives. Suppose $K\ge\kappa I$, $\kappa>0$, and $\int_0^1(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\,dt\ge\mu\int_0^1|z_t|^2\,dt$ at every label for every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\mu>0$. For every $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$, the formal statement proves unique $z,v=z_t,c,G$ satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, $z(0)=z(1)=0$, with solenoidal $z,c$ and periodic $G=\nabla\phi$. It gives a polynomial velocity bound and smoothness of $z,c,G$ for smooth data. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$; uniqueness concerns the closed interval and the gradient. The proof first solves for square-integrable time paths, then recovers time continuity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: For a prescribed common construction and $T,u,p$, the formal statement requires the data $U_j(0)$ to converge to smooth odd divergence-free $u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. It requires smooth periodic Euler evolution on $[0,T)$ with $T>0$, mean-zero pressure, odd velocity, and convergence $U_j\to u$ uniformly in the same spatial norm on every earlier $[0,S]$, $S<T$. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan with initial velocity $u(0)$ must last at least to $T$ and agree with $u$ on $[0,T)$. This is a list of required properties, not a theorem that such a solution exists. It does not quantify over an infinite maximal lifespan. The spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, where $D^if$ is the full $i$th derivative tensor in operator norm.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion: For prescribed $T,u$ and a frequency and activation schedule, the formal statement records three conditions: a single finite bound for $\|u(t)\|_\infty$ on $0\le t<T$; $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$ within that interval; and fixed real $c>0,C$ such that $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. The last condition is stronger than the printed statement of Proposition 8.2. Positivity of $T$, the Euler equations and identification of $T$ with $T_\infty$ are supplied separately. The velocity norm is an essential supremum over the unit cell. Since only sufficiently large indices occur, subtraction in the index $j-1$ has its usual meaning.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion: Given $T$ and a field $u$, the formal statement requires the following for each of $u$ and its time derivative. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and integer $m\ge0$, there is a $C^m$ field on an open neighbourhood of $K$ whose spatial derivatives through order $m$ are the uniform limits on $K$ as $t\uparrow T$ within $[0,T)$. This is the meaning of the two $C^m(K)$ limits in Proposition 8.4. The local limiting field may depend on $K$ and $m$. The time derivative is taken within the half-open lifespan. The condition itself neither proves existence of $u$ nor supplies a single jointly smooth extension in space and time.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.ReferenceSlope: For a real parameter $\varepsilon$, the formal condition says $Y(0)=1$ and $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$ for every $\tau\ge0$, where $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. This is (2.12). At zero the derivative is taken from the right. Although $Y$ is a function on all real numbers, its values at negative times are unrestricted. The condition places no sign restriction on $\varepsilon$ and proves no existence, uniqueness or growth bound. Lemma 2.5 obtains those conclusions under $0<\varepsilon\le1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd: The correction attached to $V_p$ is stored alongside that oscillation, but the paper denotes it by $C_{p+1}$. This definition recovers the paper's $C_q$ by reading the stored correction at index $q-1$. Indices are nonnegative integers: subtraction at $q=0$ gives zero rather than a negative index. Consequently $C_0$ and $C_1$ refer to the same stored entry, although only the paper's levels $q\ge1$ are used in the expansion. The condition $C_1=0$ must still be imposed or proved; it does not follow from this change of indexing.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: On $[0,T]$, profiles are smooth, one-periodic in $s$, and obey $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\mathbf d=DX^{-T}\nabla_a$, $A_1=g\mathbf aF_h$, and $S=\widetilde\chi'A_1$ in the centered cell. The requirements include $R=R_U\circ X$, $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$, $\mathsf p_1=\widetilde\chi\mathsf p[A_1]$, and $C_1=B_1=\bar q_1=0$. For $1\le p\le P$, $C_{p+1}=\mathbf d\times[-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V_p/|\kappa|^2)]$. For $2\le p\le P$, require $B_{p,t}+MB_p+\mathbf d\bar q_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$ and $V_{p,t}+MV_p+\kappa\mathsf p_{p,s}=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)+f_p^S$. Here $H_p$ is the sum of the preceding linear correction and all lower-level quadratic interactions, with the activation correction subtracted at level two; $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^p(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_s(V_{p+1-i}+C_{p+1-i})$. Means satisfy $B_p=DX\,z_{p,t}$, $\operatorname{div}_az_{p,t}=0$, $z_p(0)=z_p(T)=0$ and zero spatial pressure mean. Transverse velocities are perpendicular to $\kappa$, centered and initially zero, with centered pressure. Finally $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$. This condition asserts no existence or estimates.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed: Let $M(t,a)=\nabla U(t,X_{0,t}(a))$ and $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. A seed is a smooth field $\mathbf a$ on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ which agrees with the central seed at $a=0$, starts from $(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, and solves $\partial_t\mathbf a=-M\mathbf a+2\kappa(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$ while satisfying $\kappa\cdot\mathbf a=0$. The differential equation uses derivatives within $[t_0,T]$ at its endpoints. This records the seed equation and (5.4), not the amplitude and coupling estimates on nearby labels. Those are later conclusions. Nonvanishing of $\kappa$ comes from the parent flow and nonzero carrier, not from this declaration alone.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation: This condition identifies $u$ with $S_\Lambda V$ on $[0,T]$ by requiring the cutoff formula for every continuous function on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ representing $V$. At each time, $p$ must be smooth, periodic, have zero integral over the centered unit cell, and solve $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Existence of a continuous periodic representative of $V$ is not included in this condition: without one, its cutoff clause alone imposes no restriction. Proposition 5.11 supplies such a representative by proving $V$ smooth and periodic. The condition specifies the pressure spatially at each time; joint time smoothness is proved for the constructed truncation.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch: The conditions are $0\le t_0<T$, $k_*\ne0$, and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, with $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. They specify the activation time and the frequency convention in §5.1. Thus $\lambda$ is the length of the transported vector at the origin when the wave is activated, not automatically $|k_*|$. These conditions do not themselves assert that $X$ is a differentiable flow or that $\lambda\ge1$; those requirements are supplied by the parent hypotheses. Together with the bounds for the forward and inverse deformation, they give (5.3).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution: On $[0,T]$, let $X$ be the parent flow, $M=DU\circ X$ and $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$. The formal condition on smooth phase-independent $B,\bar q$ is $B_t+MB+\mathbf d\bar q=\bar f$, with smooth periodic fields $z,v$ satisfying $z_t=v$, $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $B=D_aXv$. Volume preservation converts this to $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, as in (5.11). The pressure’s spatial mean is not fixed here. The conditions select $B(0)$ through both displacement endpoints; they do not require zero initial velocity or vanishing before activation.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin: On $[t_0,T]$, put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|c|$. The formal conditions require $\kappa,c\ne0$, $\kappa\cdot c=0$, $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and $c_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)Mc$. For every transverse solution $b$ of the same amplitude equation and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, require $|b(t)|/|c(t)|\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/|c(t')|$, and require $\kappa\cdot Mc\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||c|$. Finally $\gamma\le1$. These are hypotheses, not an existence theorem. With $\lambda\ge1$ supplied separately, $\gamma>0$ and the stability inequality is unchanged when its denominators are replaced by $\gamma$. The paper’s stronger normalization $\max\gamma=1$ is not required.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent:
The domain is represented by periodic fields on $\mathbb R^3$. Require $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, smooth odd divergence-free $U$ with flow $X$, and Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\mathsf D$. Operator norms of $
abla U$, $D_aX$ and its inverse are at most $\mathsf D$. The pressure $p$ is smooth and periodic; $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$ is odd, supported in $|\xi|\le4\mathsf D$, and has supremum norm at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Finally $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. The time derivative is within $[0,T]$. Unlike §5.1, this condition imposes neither $\int p=0$ nor $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((
abla U)^2)$, and it does not assume $\operatorname{div}R_U=0$. The numbered results separately add $T>0$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution: Given the parent flow, its gradient $M$, transported covector $\kappa$ and forcing profile $f$, a transverse solution on $[0,T]$ satisfies $V_t+MV+\kappa\partial_s\pi=f$, $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=0$ and $V(0,a,s)=0$. The phase pressure is also normalized by $\langle\pi\rangle_s=0$. These are smooth profiles with phase period one and the simultaneous label-phase translation law giving a periodic physical field. Time derivatives hold the label fixed. This is the problem used for (1.12) after its specified forcing is inserted. The definition describes a solution; it does not assert existence, uniqueness or a bound.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The paper’s $C_p$ is stored at index $p-1$; the physical expansion sets $C_1=0$. The field $Y_p=V_p+C_p$ groups the new transverse velocity with the divergence correction produced by $V_{p-1}$. This is the convention at the start of §5.5, reflecting the extra frequency gain of the correction. The sum itself imposes no equation; its size and constraints follow from the expansion equations and Theorem 5.6.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd: For an indexed family of profiles, the formal definition gives $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ in the paper's notation. Here $C_p$ is generated by the preceding oscillation $V_{p-1}$: the stored correction index is one smaller than the paper index. The formula defines the level field used in the quadratic interactions of §1.3 and §5.5. It does not impose that $B_p$ is phase independent or that $V_p$ is transverse; these belong to the expansion equations. At index zero, subtraction is truncated to zero, so the intended mathematical use is at levels $p\ge1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection: Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, with phase period one and $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$. Nonvanishing of the transported covector is supplied by the parent geometry. The correction is $C[V]=\mathbf d\times Q[V]$, with $Q[V]=-\partial_s^{-1}((\kappa\times V)/|\kappa|^2)$. For zero-mean transverse profiles it gives $V+C[V]=\widetilde{\mathbf d}\times Q[V]$, as used in §5.5. The formal operation acts on the oscillatory part of a general profile; the divergence identity requires the zero-mean and transversality assumptions.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion: For depth $P\ge0$, the formal definition is $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$, using the paper's indices. Thus the correction of $V_P$ remains even though the next oscillation is absent. When $C_1=0$ and $P\ge1$, regrouping gives $W=\sum_{p=1}^PZ_p+C_{P+1}$; when $P=0$, the sum is empty and equals zero. The definition accepts arbitrary additive families. To obtain the approximate velocity, one evaluates the profiles at $s=k_*\cdot a$, passes to physical coordinates and adds the parent. Differential equations, divergence cancellation and size estimates are additional facts.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure: The depth $P$ is a nonnegative integer; an empty sum is zero, while Proposition 5.4 uses $P\ge2$. The profile pressure is $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^{P}(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, as in Proposition 5.4. In an admissible expansion the oscillatory pressures have zero phase mean, the mean pressures are phase independent, and $\bar q_1=0$. Those equations and normalizations belong to the construction; this expression simply adds the selected pressure components.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm: For a field $f(t,a,s)$ and time set $I$, the expression sums $\sup_{t\in I,a,s}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j(\tau(t)f)|$ over $|\alpha|+j\le n$, counting each multi-index once. Only label and phase variables are differentiated. Each supremum is implemented as a real supremum of a set that also contains zero; if that set is unbounded above, that term of the sum takes the default value zero. Thus a finite numerical value alone does not establish boundedness. Analytic estimates separately require or prove boundedness of the derivative sets. With $\tau=\gamma^{-1}$ this gives the weighted norm of Appendix D when $\gamma>0$; at a time where $\gamma(t)=0$ the multiplier $\gamma(t)^{-1}$ is zero by the convention for division by zero, so that time contributes zero. These conventions do not assert any estimate for an unbounded field or a vanishing weight.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading: For a seed field $\mathbf a(t,a)$, define $A_1(t,a,s)=g(a)\mathbf a(t,a)F_h(s)$ with $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell_*)$. The formalization selects a particular smooth radial cutoff $\chi$ and the periodic phase profile $F_h$ constructed earlier. This is the unswitched leading wave in §5.1; the time cutoff is introduced later as $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$. The formula itself assumes no differential equation for the seed and no positive radius or width. Its intended smooth localized interpretation uses $\ell_*>0$, $0<h\le1$, and the seed regularity on $[t_0,T]$ supplied in the application.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: This defines the source for $p\ge2$ using $Y_i=V_i+C_i$ and $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$; subtraction of natural-number indices is truncated at zero outside that range. The source $H_p$ contains $(\partial_t+M)C_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and the two interaction sums of (5.26). At level two it subtracts the activation contribution of the curl correction, recovering (5.25). The correction $C_p$ is already known from $V_{p-1}$, so the source does not depend on the new transverse velocity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: At level $p$, the formal definition is $\overline f_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$, where $H_p$ is the source assembled before solving for the new mean and $R$ is the supplied parent residual. In the geometric application $R=R_U\circ X$ is independent of phase. The negative sign makes the mean correction cancel the averaged error, and level two is the only place where the previous parent's residual is inserted. This is the right side of the equation described in §1.3. The definition does not solve that equation or impose the endpoint conditions selecting its initial velocity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource: For an arbitrary preliminary source $H_p$, phase averaging is the integral over one period; centering is an algebraic operation, not an existence statement. The forcing $f_p=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)$ is the centered term in (5.27). Its sign cancels the oscillatory part of $H_p$ in the momentum equation. The additional forcing $f_p^S$ is formed only after the mean solve, and the transverse equation uses their sum; centering the preliminary source alone does not include that transport.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius: The formal radius is $\ell_*=(\mathsf D^a)^{-1}$, where $a$ is a nonnegative integer. In the parent regime $\mathsf D\ge2$, this is positive; choosing $a\ge3$ gives the paper’s $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-3}$. The later estimates first fix a sufficiently large threshold for $a$, then quantify over all larger integer exponents. The radius does not change with derivative order or expansion depth. The definition also accepts $\mathsf D=0$: since the reciprocal of zero is zero, it then gives zero for $a>0$ and one for $a=0$. Those values are excluded by the parent assumptions.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder: The stored correction is indexed by its generating velocity, so the paper’s $C_{P+1}$ is the stored correction with index $P$. The expression is (5.30): the two final linear terms, label interactions with $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions with $i+j\ge P+2$. Both indices run through $P+1$, where only the final correction remains. The activation error is separate. The expansion equations are needed to identify this expression with the uncanceled momentum residual.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource: The formal definition gives $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^{p}(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$, with $Y_j=V_j+C_j$ in paper notation. In particular, at $p=2$ it is $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$ when $C_1=0$, the extra term in (1.12). The sum is empty below level two. At every included index $p+1-i\ge1$, so nonnegative-integer subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction. For phase-independent $B_i,\kappa$ and differentiable periodic $Y_j$, its phase average vanishes. These properties are not imposed by the formula alone; they come from the geometric profiles and expansion equations.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm: For a smooth profile $f$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, define $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}=\sum_{|\alpha|+j\le n}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\sup_{t\in[t_0,T],a,s}|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^jf(t,a,s)|/\gamma(t)$ for positive scales and positive $\gamma$. Each multi-index occurs once; time is not differentiated. Profiles are one-periodic in phase and obey $f(t,a+z,s+k_*\cdot z)=f(t,a,s)$ for lattice vectors $z$. In the application $0\le t_0<T$ and $\gamma$ is continuous and positive, so these suprema are finite. The unrestricted expression instead uses $|\gamma(t)^{-1}|$: division by zero is assigned zero, and an unbounded set of real derivative values has real supremum assigned zero. Consequently the unrestricted formula alone does not certify boundedness; the positivity and regularity hypotheses in the estimates are essential.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector: The formal vector is $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$, with reference time zero. When $X$ is the smooth parent flow, the inverse derivative identity makes this $(D_aX(t,a))^{-T}k_*$, exactly the transported field in §5.1. The argument $a$ is a parent label, not the physical point. The formula alone does not require $k_*\ne0$ or guarantee invertibility: these enter through the parent and activation hypotheses. Likewise, nonvanishing and the frequency comparisons (5.3) are proved separately. Outside differentiability, the formal derivative expression is assigned its default value zero.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight: Given a frequency $\lambda$ and central seed $\mathbf a(t,0)$, define $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. This is the weight used in the active-interval profile norms: $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$ measures spatial and phase derivatives of $f/\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$. Because $\gamma$ depends only on time, those derivatives do not act on it. The definition itself proves neither positivity nor an upper bound. The parent frequency $\lambda\ge1$, nonzero central seed, and normalization imposed elsewhere give $0<\gamma\le1$. It does not impose the paper’s stronger equality $\max_{[t_0,T]}\gamma=1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width: The formal width is the real power $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. Under the parent condition $\lambda\ge1$, this gives $0<h\le1$, as required for the chosen periodic profile $F_h$. In the finite profile norms, every phase derivative carries a factor $h$; converting to a physical derivative introduces $|k_*|h^{-1}$. With $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$ this is at most $\mathsf D\lambda^{3/2}$. The width definition does not assert these inequalities without their frequency assumptions. Combined with central amplitude scale $\lambda^{-3/4}$ and $\|F_h\|_\infty=O(h)$, it yields the leading velocity scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$.

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep: Fix $P'\le P$ and the same numerical recurrence coefficient $K$ in both depths. The equality holds for every $q\le P'$. The numerical constant for a level is unchanged when the surrounding expansion is extended to a larger depth. The interaction pairs at the earlier levels are identical, so induction gives equality of their constants. This justifies the dependence $C_{n,p}$ in Theorem 5.6; it does not assert a bound uniform in $p$.

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oddExpansions_of: Assume Proposition 5.4, including uniqueness of the retained profiles. Over the smooth odd periodic parent of §5.1, take a seed with even dependence on the label and an admissible depth-$P\ge2$ expansion. Reflect $(a,s)$ to $(-a,-s)$, reverse the sign of velocity profiles and preserve the sign of pressure profiles. The reflected family satisfies the same defining equations and prescribed data. Uniqueness therefore makes the retained velocity expansion odd under this reflection. After composition with the odd inverse parent flow, its Eulerian perturbation is odd. This statement proves symmetry of the expansion; it does not derive its quantitative estimates or bound its residual.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm: The profile is smooth and phase periodic, with the coupled label-translation law; the weight is continuous on the compact active interval. For a profile vanishing before $t_0$, its unweighted norm on $[0,T]$ is at most its weighted norm on $[t_0,T]$ when $0<\gamma\le1$. The vanishing assumption matters because the time intervals differ. The remainder proof applies this to terms containing oscillations; products of two means are estimated directly in the unweighted norm.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general: Let $\ell_*,h>0$ and let the time weight $\gamma$ be positive. Suppose all finite norms of $f/\gamma$ exist, and the coefficients of label and phase differentiation have finite order-$j$ bounds $N_c(j)$ and $N_k(j)$. Assuming the finite-norm product estimate, the sum over all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is bounded by $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j(9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}+3N_k(j)h^{-1})]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The formal conclusion also includes finiteness of these differentiated norms. With inverse-flow coefficients and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, this gives the derivative cost in Lemma 5.7. The product for $m=0$ is one; its order constants are those of the product estimate, not new assumptions on the parent.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep: Let $f$ be independent of phase, $\ell_*,h>0$, and $\gamma>0$. Assume finite weighted profile norms at every order and finite order-$j$ coefficient bounds $N_c(j),N_k(j)$ for the label and phase parts of the derivative operator. Given the finite-norm product estimate, the sum of the weighted norms after all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is at most $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The phase-coefficient bounds remain formal premises, but no $N_k(j)h^{-1}$ factor appears in the conclusion because phase derivatives vanish. This is the improved mean estimate used in Lemma 5.7. The conclusion includes finiteness of all differentiated order-zero norms.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L: For a real-valued frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, the formal definition is $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. This is the gain parameter in (1.14); in particular $L_{j+1}$ uses $\lambda_{j+2}$, which matters in Lemma 1.3. The formula is defined even without a positive-frequency hypothesis. The logarithm is assigned the value zero at zero and is extended to negative arguments using their absolute value. In the paper’s schedule all frequencies exceed one, so this convention is inactive and $L_j>0$. The formula alone provides neither that positivity nor any bound on the gain.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε: For the frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal definition assigns $\varepsilon_j=1/L_{j+1}^2$, agreeing with $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$ for $j\ge2$ in (1.14). Consequently $\varepsilon_j$ depends on $\lambda_{j+2}$, not $\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal formula also assigns a value at index zero, which this part of the paper does not use. Division by zero is assigned the value zero, so a zero gain would give a zero ratio, not an infinite one. The positive-frequency schedule supplies positive gains; separate estimates make these positive ratios small enough for amplification.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ: For a positive frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. At each wave index $j\ge1$, the formal definition is $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$, the half-length used in $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$. The formula uses a real exponent $-1/8$ and an integer cube. It is also assigned a value at index zero: subtraction of one from a nonnegative integer gives zero there, so it uses $\lambda_0$. The paper does not use that extra value. Positivity, decay of $\tau_j$, and the endpoint relation require separate assertions; this formula alone supplies none of them.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension: The formal condition asks for an open set containing $\{T\}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ and a field $g$ smooth jointly on its union with $[0,T)\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$. The field is periodic under every integer spatial translation and equals $u$ on that entire preterminal punctured slab. Thus it descends to a smooth extension through the terminal slice of the punctured torus. The field is defined everywhere, but smoothness is required only on the stated union; its other values are unconstrained. This condition neither asserts an Euler equation after $T$ nor extends a pressure. It specifies what an extension means and does not prove one exists.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13: Let $F=D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$ for the parent flow on $[0,T]$. The formal condition assumes $T>0$ and the standing hypotheses of §5.1: $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, $U$ smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free with frequencies at most $2\mathsf D$, the bounds (5.1), $R_U$ odd with frequencies at most $4\mathsf D$ and $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and the coercivity (5.2); the pressure may be any smooth periodic pressure whose residual has these properties. For each nonnegative integer $C_A$, the assertion selects $a_0$; for every integer $a\ge a_0$ it selects $C$ and $C_m$, independently of the parent and derivative order. For $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and every $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$, it asserts finiteness and $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for all $m\ge1$. Each Hölder norm is the maximum of its uniform norm and seminorm, over all labels and times in $[0,T]$. This defines the proposed assertion; the linked proof establishes it from Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.2 and (D.2).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14:
Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Write $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Let smooth periodic $B,z, ar q, ar f$ satisfy $B_t+MB+F^{-T}
abla_a ar q= ar f$, $B=Fz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. Put $v=F^{-1}B=z_t$ and $g=F^T ar f$. For sufficiently large fixed $a$, $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, and finite scaled source half-Hölder norm, the formal statement gives finiteness of the velocity norm and $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$ for all $n\ge0$. The norms sum scaled label derivatives on the whole interval, with the maximum of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm at each order. The exponent $C$ is chosen after $a$ but before the parent and derivative order.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59: For each integer $m\ge0$, the assertion asks for a nonnegative constant $C_m$ such that every continuous bilinear map $B:E\times F\to G$ between real normed spaces satisfies $\|B(f,g)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$ whenever $f:\mathbb R^3\to E$ and $g:\mathbb R^3\to F$ belong to $C^{m,1/2}$. The output’s Hölder regularity is also asserted. The constant is chosen before the spaces, fields and bilinear map. This states a generalization of (5.59); scalar multiplication and the tensor products used in §5.7 are particular cases. It does not require periodicity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement asserts $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At an order $m$ with derivatives bounded through $m+1$, it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for. The proof is supplied separately.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8: The formal statement asks for parameters, an inductive construction, a constant and a real time $T$ satisfying the conclusions of Theorem 7.1. These include smooth odd divergence-free periodic stage velocities, the residual and central-wave bounds, summable corrections, shrinking oscillation supports, and $0<T<S_j$ for every stage, with $t_j\to T$. Thus $T$ is the paper’s common accumulation time. This declaration specifies an existence assertion; the adjoining proof establishes it from Theorem 7.1. Its conclusion contains no limiting field and no uniform convergence on $[0,T]$. It represents only the initial choice in Section 8, not the whole opening paragraph.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.corollary_8_3: Given a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit $u,p$ from Proposition 8.1, assume bounded velocity, central vorticity blow-up, and fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ throughout every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. The formal statement concludes maximality at $T_\infty>0$, equality with the lifespan of every other maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$, and divergence of both integrals in (1.2). The quantitative bound is included in the formal Proposition 8.2, although not in its printed statement. This declaration specifies the implication; its proof uses crossing durations instead of a general continuation criterion. The integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals over the half-open lifespan.

Means need not vanish before activation. Smoothness is on the closed slab; no continuation across its endpoints is asserted.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: For every common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, the formal statement asserts existence of smooth periodic velocity and mean-zero pressure solving Euler on $[0,T_\infty)$. The limiting datum $u(0)$ is smooth, odd and divergence free; $U_j(0)\to u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. For each $S<T_\infty$, convergence to $u$ is uniform on $[0,S]$ in every such spatial norm, and $u$ remains odd. Any maximal solution with the same data and a finite lifespan must last at least to $T_\infty$ and agree there. Unlike the paper’s formulation, existence of a general maximal solution is not assumed or concluded. This declaration states the assertion; a separate theorem proves it. The precise numerical Hölder norm is defined in an omitted file.

For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement asserts bounded velocity on $[0,T_\infty)$ and the full limit $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. It also asserts fixed real $c>0,C$ such that $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Here the spatial domain is represented by period-one fields on $\mathbb R^3$, and the velocity norm is the essential supremum on one unit cell. The interval estimate is extra information beyond the printed Proposition 8.2. This declaration specifies the assertion; its proof and its application to integral divergence are separate.

For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth periodic Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement asserts both limits in Proposition 8.4. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and integer $m\ge0$, $u(t)$ and its time derivative converge uniformly on $K$ with all spatial derivatives through order $m$, as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. Each limiting field is $C^m$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. The removed lattice is precisely the set of representatives of the torus origin. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T_\infty)$. This declaration states the implication; it does not itself prove it. No single jointly smooth extension through the terminal time is required by this conclusion.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.remark_1_2: There exist smooth odd divergence-free data $u_0$ on $\mathbb T^3$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, with $0<T_*<\infty$, bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and divergent time integrals of both gradient and vorticity norms. Velocity and its time derivative converge in every spatial $C^m$ norm on compact sets away from the origin. The velocity also extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from that point. Any maximal solution from $u_0$ has the same lifespan and velocity. The extension is periodic and need not solve Euler after $T_*$. This is the existential assertion of Remark 1.2, not an extension theorem for every singular solution.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1: There exist smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$, with finite $T_*>0$. Velocity remains uniformly bounded, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and the time integrals of $\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty$ and $\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty$ both diverge. For every compact set away from the torus origin and every $m\ge0$, velocity and its time derivative converge in $C^m$. The formal statement further spells out the classical uniqueness implicit in the paper: every maximal solution from $u_0$ has endpoint $T_*$ and agrees with $u$ before it. Fields are periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$; pressure has zero spatial mean.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_4_2: On $I=[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, let $U$ be smooth, unit-periodic and divergence free, $X$ its flow from time zero, $F=D_aX$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, and $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. Assume $\|F^{-1}\|_\infty\le D\ge1$, $\|M\|_\infty\le L$, $\|K\|_\infty\le K_0$, $\|D_aK\|_\infty\le K_1$, $\|\Omega\|_\infty\le\Omega_0$, $\|D_a\Omega\|_\infty\le\Omega_1$, with nonnegative bounds. For $L_{\rm src}\in C(I;C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3))$, solve $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L_{\rm src}=c+G_\phi$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, where $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. The fields $z,v,c$ are weakly divergence free; $z\in C^1_tC^{0,1/2}$, $v,G_\phi\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$, and $G_\phi=\nabla_a\phi$ for a periodic potential at each time. There are absolute $C\ge0$ and an integer $p\ge0$ such that $A=C(D+L+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^p$ gives $\|v\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le A\|L_{\rm src}\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}$ and $\|(\mathbb PK(t))^{-1}\mathbb P\|\le A$ uniformly on $I$. The solution is unique in $z,v,c,G_\phi$ on $I$, not in the potential. Smooth force sources $L_{\rm src}=-J(F^T(f\circ X))$ also give smooth solutions of the linearized Euler equation. The coefficient bound uses first derivative suprema rather than full $C^{1,1/2}$ norms.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6: Assume smooth odd periodic solenoidal $U$ and smooth periodic $p_U$ on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. Take sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and a depth-$P$ expansion, $P\ge2$. If $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, for $1\le p\le P$ and every order the transverse velocity, forcing and $\lambda$ times pressure have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$; means and mean sources, for $p\ge2$, have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2-2(p-2)/3}$; $C_{p+1}$ has size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-9/4-2(p-1)/3}$. The oscillatory sum is $\le C_{m,P}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}$ in the weighted norm, and the summed mean and mean-source norms are $\le C_{m,P}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $\|R_P\|_{[m]}\le C_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. Mean norms use $[0,T]$; weighted norms use $[t_0,T]$. One exponent covers all orders, levels and depths.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: For every smooth radial Fourier cutoff and integer $a_0$, the formal statement chooses $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and fixed-order majorants before an admissible threshold $\mathcal B$. Every such threshold permits the construction for all sufficiently large $N$. It asserts smooth odd divergence-free periodic velocities on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $\|U_j\|_\infty,\|(D_aX_j)^{\pm1}\|_\infty\le\lambda_j$, $\|R_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ and $D^2\pi_j\le(\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1})I$. The central splitting has error $\le\lambda_j^{-1/4}$; at $t_{j+1}$, $\eta_j/\nu_j=\varepsilon_j$, $\pi\le\nu_j\le4\pi$ and $C^{-1}\lambda_j^{1/4}\le\sigma_j\le C\lambda_j^{1/4}L_{j+1}^2$, with $C=18e^3$. Localized increments satisfy $\|O_j\|_\infty,\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for $m\le q_j$, and $t_j\to T_\infty\in(0,S_j)$. Each increment is identified with its finite expansion and Fourier truncation. The central amplitude is identified with the seed; the central covector is not identified with its transported counterpart, and first-wave directions and attained normalization are absent. The exponent quantifier is $\forall a_0\,\exists a\ge a_0$. Hölder estimates are stated at each time, in the spatial norm $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, with $D^if$ the full $i$th derivative tensor. This declaration states the assertion, not its proof.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: There are constants $C\ge0$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, chosen before the data. On $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$, let symmetric $K$ and skew-symmetric $\Omega$ be time-continuous in $C^{0,1/2}$ and spatially differentiable, with uniform value and first derivative bounds $K_0,K_1,\Omega_0,\Omega_1$. Assume $K\ge\kappa I$, $\kappa>0$, and $\int_0^1(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\,dt\ge\mu\int_0^1|z_t|^2\,dt$ for every $H^1_0$ path at every label, with $\mu>0$. Each $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$ gives unique $z,v=z_t,c,G$ on this interval satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, $z(0)=z(1)=0$, with solenoidal $z,c$ and periodic $G=\nabla\phi$. Moreover $\|v\|_0\le CQ^p\|L\|_0$, where $Q=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1$ and $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw$. Smooth data give smooth $z,c,G$. The norm is the time supremum of the spatial half-Hölder norm. The paper assumes stronger coefficient regularity; the scalar potential is not unique.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Write $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Fix an integer $C_A\ge0$. For every sufficiently large fixed integer $a$, put $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$. For every $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$ and every integer $m\ge1$, the formal statement gives finite coefficient half-Hölder norms and $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$. Here $|\cdot|_{m,1/2}$ sums order-$m$ coordinate derivative half-Hölder norms uniformly over the closed interval. The radius threshold may depend on $C_A$, but not on $m$; after $a$ is fixed, $C$ and $C_m$ precede the parent and $A$.

Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
